chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Abbas Fadl al-Baqbaq from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'Do women have qawd (blood money) or 'afw (compensation)?' He said, 'No, and that is for the 'asabah (male agnates).'
Ali ibn al-Hasan said, 'This is contrary to what our companions hold.'

key_terms.عَصَبَة: Male agnates (paternal relatives entitled to inheritance/compensation)
key_terms.قَوَد: Blood money or compensation for injury/death

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to receive blood money or compensation for women according to this Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the right to claim blood money (diya) or forgive the perpetrator lies exclusively with the 'asabah (male agnates), excluding women from this specific legal authority. This narration highlights a key jurisprudential divergence (khilaf) between the Imami school and other contemporary scholars regarding the distribution of inheritance and compensation rights. It underscores the distinct Shia interpretation of kinship-based legal agency in cases of homicide or injury.
